summary: James W. Benson is an indologist and linguist who held posts at Harvard University and the University of Oxford (both attested in 1999), as well as Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2001). His students include James McHugh and Susan J. Rosenfield.

James W. Heisig, a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology, earned degrees from Divine Word College, Loyola University Chicago, Notre Dame, and Cambridge. He held several posts at Nanzan University, serving as its director from 1991 to 2001.

James Ward (1843–1925) was a philosopher who studied at Mostyn House School, Fitzwilliam College (~1869–1872), and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1872–1875). He held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1897–1925) and taught Surendranath Dasgupta.
James Whitehill works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He founded the Columbia Zen Center and served as Professor of Religion at Stephens College (attested in 2000).

James Wilson Bright (1852–1926) was a linguist who studied at Lafayette College and earned his PhD from Johns Hopkins University. He taught at Cornell (~1885) and held the Caroline Donovan Chair of English at Johns Hopkins from 1905 to 1925.

Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso (1846–1912) was a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology scholar. He studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and taught numerous students, such as Shechen Gyaltsab and Ngorpa Pönlob Lo Ter Wangpo.

Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge (1954–1992) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under the 16th Karmapa, Kalu Rinpoche, Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, and taught Richard Barron and Jampa Mackenzie Stewart.

Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye (1813–1899) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied under teachers such as Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Tekchok Dorje, and Gyurme Thutop Namgyal, and taught disciples including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa.

Jamie Hubbard is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Komazawa University and under Minoru Kiyota at the University of Wisconsin–Madison (PhD). At Smith College (attested 2016), he held endowed professorships in religion and East Asian studies.

Jampa Losang Panglung (1939–2022) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who trained at Sera Monastery and the University of Munich. From around 1980 to 2005, he held research and editorial positions at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Jampa Mackenzie Stewart works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge and Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche (attested in 1995).

Jampa Samten is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He worked as a bibliographer at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 1987) and served as Director (attested 2003–2004) and Professor (attested 2015) at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Jampal Kunzang Rechung (born 1930) is a Tibetology scholar. He served as editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1980–1988) and as Deputy Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1982).

Jamsrangiin Tseveen (1881–1942) was a scholar of linguistics, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Saint Petersburg (~1902–1906) and worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (1932–1937).

Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö (1893–1959) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied under teachers including Khenpo Thupten and Shechen Gyaltsab, succeeded Jamyang Chökyi Wangpo, and taught figures such as Namkhai Norbu, Dilgo Khyentse, and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje.

Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (1820–1892) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under teachers including Minling Trichen Gyurme Sangye Kunga and Shechen Gyurme Thutob Namgyal, and taught disciples such as Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Jamyang Sherab Chokyi Nangwa was a student who studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Jan A. Schoterman (1948–1989) was an indologist who studied at Utrecht University (attested 1982) under doctoral supervisor Henk Bodewitz and teacher Jan Gonda.

Jan Chozen Bays (b. 1945), a Buddhist studies and religious studies practitioner, studied under Taizan Maezumi and Shodo Harada. She founded Great Vow Zen Monastery (serving as abbess ~2002) and Heart of Wisdom Zen Temple.
Jan Dolensky is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2013).
